# `thindata`: keep at most one point per cell {#sec-thindata}

## What it does

`thindata` reduces point density by keeping at most one point in each
grid cell. It is used to make data from different acquisitions comparable
(for example, thinning a dense recent flight to match an older, sparser
one), to test how sensitive a model is to point density, or to shrink a
point cloud for quick viewing.

The grid lines fall on whole multiples of the cell size in the data's own
coordinates, so thinning two adjacent tiles gives one consistent grid
across both.

## Example commands

{{< include ../examples/fragments/thindata_commands.md >}}

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| `/output` | `out/thindata.las` | The thinned point cloud. |
| `/cellsize` | `2` | Keep at most one point per 2 x 2 ft cell. |

: Options used in the `thindata` example. {#tbl-options-thindata}

The `/class` and `/return` filters (@sec-point-filtering) are applied
before thinning, so `/return:first /cellsize:2` keeps at most one first
return per cell.

## Outputs

One LAS or LAZ file with the same point format and coordinate system as
the input, holding one point for every occupied cell.

## Results

@fig-thindata-window zooms in on a 20 x 20 ft patch in the middle of the
tile. Grey points are the original tile, orange points are the ones kept,
and the grid lines are the 2 ft thinning grid. Every square that holds
grey points holds exactly one orange point.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/thindata_figures.md >}}

## Checks

@tbl-checks-thindata confirms that no cell keeps more than one point,
that the number kept equals the number of occupied cells, and that every
kept point is an original point rather than a new, averaged one.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/thindata_checks.md >}}
